title: Secant slopes and right-hand liminf
statement: Let $f\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfy $f(0)=0$, be continuous at $0$, and obey $f(s+t)\le f(s)+f(t)$ for all $s,t\in\mathbb R$. For every $\delta>0$, the extended nonnegative real number obtained by truncating $f(\delta)/\delta$ below at zero is at most $\liminf_{t\to0^+}$ of the similarly truncated quotients $f(t)/t$.
replaced: Let $f\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be continuous at zero with $f(0)=0$ and $f(s+t)\le f(s)+f(t)$ for all real $s,t$. Then for every $\delta>0$, $[f(\delta)/\delta]_+\le\liminf_{t\to0^+}[f(t)/t]_+$ in $[0,\infty]$, where $[u]_+=\max(u,0)$.
